newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Le Pen threatens election night boycott.
newsitem.headline: France's Le Pen threatens election night boycott.

text.p: French extreme rightist leader Jean-Marie Le Pen threatened on Thursday that his party would boycott election-night television shows in protest against what he called the muzzling of his National Front's campaign.

"I adressed 3,000 people in Marseille yesterday and there was not a word on television, at least not on the state-owned channel which reported the campaign meetings of (Gaullist) Philippe Seguin and (Communist) Robert Hue who spoke to skeleton audiences," Le Pen told Radio Monte Carlo.
"This is an absolute scandal, more typical of a banana republic and we're not going to accept such undemocratic methods," the anti-immigration crusader said.
"I'm going to propose to the executive committee that we stay away from TV stations on election night (Sunday) to bring home to the French people what is happening," he said.

Election night debates with the main political leaders after the first round of France's two-stage general election are closely watched for pointers to the positions the parties will adopt for the runoff round the following week.
There have been conflicting statements by National Front leaders about how their backers should vote where their own candidates do not qualify for the second round.
Le Pen repeated on Thursday that, if his own party did not win, he would prefer the left to win the elections since this would create more problems for President Jacques Chirac.
"I've been fighting against the left for 50 years so I don't find anything abnormal in the positions which they hold. But the (centre) right are traitors and I execrate their treason," he said.

Other FN leaders have said they disagree and that the left must be considered their main enemy to be beaten at all costs. Le Pen's boycott proposal could be an attempt to keep would-be successors from making their positions too widely known.
Le Pen added that France would repudiate the Maastricht treaty on European unity it approved by referendum in 1992 if he came to power.
"Of course we can repudiate it. If you put your neck in a noose by mistake you are allowed to cut the rope. It's legitimate defence," he said.
